title: Ulyana and the Protocol
premise: Hazel Galloway has spent a decade smuggling memories past orbital customs and quietly maintaining a beacon whose original owner vanished before he was born. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, he discovers the beacon is a dead man's switch left by Ulyana Voss, the last speaker of that tongue, whose consciousness still runs inside the relay at the edge of dead space. Racing corporate salvagers who want to strip the relay for its archived minds, Hazel must choose between selling the signal and honoring an inheritance he never asked for. In the end he reaches the relay, frees Ulyana's archived community into the open network, and burns his smuggling career to do it—finding the found family he never had in the voices of the dead.
about_author: Freya Galloway is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who left academia after a decade of listening to signals nobody answered. She writes near-future science fiction about people who keep things running long after everyone stops caring.

chapters.title: Contraband Hearts
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. A routine memory-smuggling run through orbital customs nearly goes wrong when a client's grief-recording triggers a scanner anomaly. Hazel buys his way out with a bribe and a lie, establishing his world: transactional, lonely, precise. Emotional beat: competence masking exhaustion; he trusts no one, including himself.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Back at his station, Hazel performs maintenance on the ancient beacon he's kept alive for years—a habit inherited from his missing mentor, Corvo. He finds a maintenance log entry dated tomorrow. Emotional beat: uncanny dread; the inheritance he tends may be tending him back.

chapters.title: A Language of Ash
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. The beacon receives a distress signal in Kessari, a language extinct two centuries. Linguistic archives confirm no living speaker exists—yet the syntax is alive, evolving mid-transmission. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear; something impossible is asking for help.

chapters.title: Ulyana
chapters.summary: POV Hazel, with fragments of Ulyana's archived logs. Decoding reveals the sender's name: Ulyana Voss, the beacon's original commissioner, whose mind runs inside the edge-of-dead-space relay with hundreds of other archived refugees. Emotional beat: grief and connection; Hazel realizes he's been corresponding with a ghost all along.

chapters.title: Buyers
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. The Halcyon Combine's salvage division learns of the signal and offers Hazel a fortune to hand over the beacon's core. His debts, his ship's failing drive, and his isolation all argue yes. Emotional beat: temptation; loyalty versus survival becomes a price tag.

chapters.title: Dead Space Rules
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Hazel refuses and flees toward the relay, but the Combine tags his ship. En route he decodes more of Ulyana's archive—recordings of a persecuted community that chose digital exile over erasure. Emotional beat: resolve hardening; he recognizes his own hiding in theirs.

chapters.title: What Corvo Left Me
chapters.summary: POV Hazel, flashback-heavy. A hidden partition in the beacon opens, revealing Corvo was Ulyana's last student and chose Hazel as heir deliberately. The 'tomorrow' log entry was Corvo's final message, sent posthumously through the beacon. Emotional beat: betrayal transmuted into belonging; he was chosen, not abandoned.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. The Combine catches Hazel at the last jump gate. He sacrifices his cargo—every contraband memory he owns—to buy escape, scattering clients' secrets into open space as cover. Emotional beat: costly sacrifice; the smuggler destroys his own livelihood to keep a promise.

chapters.title: The Relay at the End of Everything
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. At the dying relay, Hazel meets Ulyana's fragmented consciousness and finds the Combine's salvage fleet minutes behind. To free the archived minds, someone must merge with the relay's failing core and broadcast them outward. Emotional beat: terror and clarity at the threshold of self-erasure.

chapters.title: Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Hazel, closing with Ulyana's voice. Hazel merges with the core just long enough to release the archive into the network; Ulyana holds the door while he withdraws, diminished but alive. The Combine arrives to find an empty relay and a sky full of new voices. Emotional beat: quiet triumph; truth delivered, family found, inheritance honored.
